definitions.explanation: One of the individual leaf-like parts that make up the head of a flower. A common word in everyday Japanese and frequently used in poetic and literary imagery.

examples.japanese: {桜|さくら}の{花|はな}びらが{散|ち}っている。
{風|かぜ}に{乗|の}って{花|はな}びらが{舞|ま}い{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: Petals danced up on the wind.

examples.japanese: {水面|すいめん}に{浮|う}かんだ{花|はな}びらが{美|うつく}しい{模様|もよう}を{作|つく}っていた。
examples.english: The petals floating on the water's surface formed a beautiful pattern.

notes:
USAGE:
One of the most common nature words in Japanese. {桜|さくら}の{花|はな}びら (cherry blossom petals) is an iconic image in Japanese culture and poetry. The word is native Japanese (wago) and is usually written in kana for びら, though the kanji {花弁|はなびら} exists.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {花|はな}びらが{散|ち}る: petals fall/scatter
- {花|はな}びらが{舞|ま}う: petals flutter/dance
- {花|はな}びらが{浮|う}かぶ: petals float
- {桜|さくら}の{花|はな}びら: cherry blossom petals
- {薔薇|ばら}の{花|はな}びら: rose petals
